sanskrit: yadā ca citraḥ saṃnīto yamadūtaiḥ surapriye | saśarīro mahāprājño yamādeśaparāyaṇaiḥ || 2 || evaṃ jñātvā tu tatrasthā bhaginī tasya duḥkhitā | citrā nadī tato bhūtvā svasā tasya mahātmanaḥ || 3 || praviṣṭā sāgare devi anveṣantī ca bāṃdhavam | tataścitrapathānāma tasyāścakrurdvijātayaḥ || 4 ||
english: O beloved goddess of Suras, when the highly intelligent Citra was bodily carried off by the messengers of Yama carrying out his behests, his sister who was there came to know of it. She became extremely miserable. O goddess, the sister of that noble-souled one became the river Citrā and entered the great ocean in search of her kinsman (brother). Brāhmaṇas assigned her the name Citrapathā. It was in this manner, O lady of excellent complexion, that the river came to flow there.
